issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a public constructor for Ride that accepts both attributes in order (name: String, abbreviation: char). The solution implementation provides only Ride(String name) (setting abbreviation to a default), while RollerCoaster's constructor calls super(name, abbreviation). This creates a mismatch/compilation error and contradicts the specified constructor signature, preventing students from following the UML/requirements.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure Ride declares a public constructor with the parameters (String name, char abbreviation) and assigns both fields accordingly, matching the UML and problem statement. Alternatively, make the RollerCoaster constructor call a matching super(...) signature, but the preferred fix is to align Ride with the specified attribute order so subclasses can call super(name, abbreviation).
